Chapter Details: Status of digitalisation of records in rural facilities
Definition: The status of digital data capture in rural primary healthcare clinics
Comments: Cabo Verde has implemented DHIS2 for health management information system, including trackers for 18 programs (WHO AFRO-funded) and used for COVID surveillance/vaccines, indicating aggregate digital reporting from facilities including rural island clinics DHIS2 Community Forum, DIAL Exchange. WHO CCS 2024-2028 prioritizes strengthening digital health, modernizing HIS/DHIS2, but notes challenges in data timeliness/quality and lack of integrated digital strategy; no evidence of EMR or digital patient records (registers, prescriptions) at primary/rural clinics WHO CCS. Rural clinics likely use paper records with aggregate entry at higher levels, fitting score 2 (predominantly paper, some digital aggregate/pilots). No paper-specific confirmation found, but absence of EMR evidence in advanced system supports this over higher scores.

revision_notes: Original cited sources (DHIS2 forum thread, DIAL project page, WHO Country Cooperation Strategy) confirm only aggregate/programme-level digital reporting via DHIS2, consistent with a facility-level paper baseline; the row's own Comments text argued for score 2 while Value Code was recorded as 1, an internal inconsistency. A 2023 Ministry of Health TOR document explicitly states the single-patient digital record (M1) is used only in Praia health facilities, not on the rural islands, while DHIS2 nationwide is aggregate-only - directly supporting a facility-level paper baseline outside the capital. However, fresh evidence of an active national telemedicine programme (24 units delivered by December 2025, per Balai.cv and Brava.news reporting from April and December 2025) shows island/rural clinics now digitally capturing and transmitting diagnostic images (X-ray, ECG, ultrasound), which is genuine facility-level digital data capture beyond mere aggregate reporting. This supports moving the score up one band to 2 (Mostly paper - some digital) rather than confirming 1.
revised_comments: Cabo Verde's health information system remains only partially digitised at the point of care. A 2023 Ministry of Health technical assessment confirms that the single digital patient record application (M1) is used exclusively in health facilities in the capital, Praia, while DHIS2 is used nationwide but only for aggregate and programme-level reporting rather than primary clinical data capture. The National Digital Health Strategy 2024-2034 and a WHO-supported assessment place the health information system at roughly 55% maturity, and the government has since rolled out telemedicine units (24 delivered by December 2025) enabling digital transmission of X-rays, ECGs and ultrasound images between island clinics and central hospitals. Rural clinics therefore continue to rely predominantly on paper-based patient records, supplemented by a growing but still limited set of digital tools for diagnostics and aggregate reporting.

Definition: The status of digital data capture in rural police stations
Comments: No specific evidence found of digital recording of case files, complaints, or incident reports at rural police stations/posts. National Police has regional commands and posts on rural islands (e.g., Santo Antão, Fogo). Recent SIJ judicial system (2026) integrates police with courts for process tracking but focuses on court-level digitalisation, not initial station recording. US State Dept HR reports and UNODC training mention no station-level digital tools. General gov digital push exists, but rural police likely use paper for initial data collection, consistent with many African countries absent contrary evidence. Score 1 as broad paper use indicated.

revision_notes: The cited US State Department human rights report URL returned a dead/forbidden link and could not be verified. The remaining cited sources (Terra Nova, Wikipedia) describe only the court-level launch of the SIJ system and general police organisation, not facility-level digitisation, so the original score of 1 was reasonably cautious given what was cited. However, subsequent official reporting from the Instituto da Modernização e Inovação da Justiça (IMIJ, a government body) and the justica.gov.cv portal, dated March-May 2026, states explicitly that the SIJ platform is now integrated with National Police stations and Judicial Police delegations, that complaint handling is 'essentially digital, from the police to the courts', and that the system is operational in 14 of the country's judicial comarcas (covering most islands/municipalities), with only the small island of Brava still pending due to local network infrastructure. This is authoritative, current, and specific enough to justify raising the score from 1 to 3, since digital case data capture now appears to reach the great majority of rural/island police stations, short of full nationwide (target 2027) coverage.
revised_comments: Cabo Verde's Sistema de Informacao da Justica (SIJ), launched in January 2025 by the Nucleo Operacional da Sociedade de Informacao (NOSi) and the Instituto da Modernizacao e Inovacao da Justica (IMIJ), integrates National Police stations and Judicial Police delegations directly with the courts, giving each criminal case a unique digital reference number. By May 2026 the platform is operational in 14 of the country's judicial comarcas, covering the great majority of islands and municipalities, with only the small island comarca of Brava awaiting full integration pending local network upgrades. Official reporting states that complaint handling is now 'essentially digital, from the police to the courts', with roughly 25,000 police reports and over 18,000 cases processed digitally to date. Rural and island police stations therefore now capture and transmit case data digitally across most of the country, though a residual paper-based process persists in the least-connected areas and full nationwide coverage, targeted for 2027, is not yet complete.

Chapter Details: Status of digitalisation of records in rural facilities
Definition: The status of digital data capture in rural civil registry offices
Comments: Cabo Verde has one of Africa's most robust CRVS systems, with nearly 100% death certification by doctors and significant integration of information systems for vital statistics. WHO assessment highlights progress in CRVS, with recommendations for real-time digitization and IT reinforcement, indicating predominantly digital operations with some paper elements. National SNIAC system coordinates civil identification and registration, providing electronic authentication, digital signatures, and integration with health, education, etc. Government sites mention online requests for certificates via portals like Porton di Nos Ilha and consular platforms (100% digital processes). High birth registration completeness (~91% per World Bank). No explicit rural-specific evidence found, but centralized digital infrastructure (SNIAC aims for national coverage including diaspora) suggests rural registry points use digital systems, though initial recording may involve paper in remote areas. Score 3 as predominantly digital nationally, with ongoing digitization.

revision_notes: All four originally cited sources were fetched and are genuine and relevant, though none give rural-specific detail, as the row itself acknowledged. The founding law of SNIAC (Law 43/VIII/2013) confirms that civil registry offices (conservatorias do registo civil) nationwide are the designated digital collection points for biographic and biometric data, including a mobile registration service for citizens unable to travel to a fixed office, which supports genuinely national (not just capital-based) digital data capture at registry level. A May 2025 WHO-supported assessment corroborates this as one of the strongest CRVS systems in Africa, while still recommending further real-time digitisation of notifications, indicating the system is not yet entirely digital. The evidence supports confirming the existing score of 3 rather than promoting to the top of the scale, since gaps in real-time notification (particularly for deaths outside hospitals) remain documented as recently as 2025.
revised_comments: Cabo Verde's civil registry offices (conservatorias do registo civil) function as designated collection points for the Sistema Nacional de Identificacao e Autenticacao Civil (SNIAC), a centralised digital platform established by Law 43/VIII/2013 that captures biographic and biometric data for births, deaths, marriages and other vital events directly at the point of registration, including via mobile registration units for citizens unable to travel. A May 2025 WHO-supported national assessment describes Cabo Verde's civil registration and vital statistics system as one of the most robust in Africa, with almost 100% of deaths certified by a doctor, while recommending further work on real-time digitisation of notifications and IT reinforcement, particularly for death registration outside the main hospitals. This indicates that registry offices, including those on the smaller and more rural islands, operate on a predominantly digital basis, with residual manual steps in notification and reporting rather than in core data capture.

Chapter Details: Status of digitalisation of records in rural facilities
Definition: The status of digital data capture in rural primary schools
Comments: Rural primary schools in Cabo Verde use the SIGE (Sistema Integrado de Gestão Escolar), a digital platform rolled out nationally by 2019 to all 395 basic education schools, including rural ones across the territory, for recording attendance, grades, administrative data, and enabling online parental access. This indicates digital systems are standard at point of service for admin and attendance. National EMIS/SIGE supports evidence-based decisions with real-time data. Digital initiatives like computer distribution to all basic schools (2021) and WebLabs enhance capacity. However, rural-urban gaps persist in internet access, device ownership, and connectivity (Afrobarometer 2020; World Bank 2020), with some reliance on printed materials in low-coverage areas during COVID, suggesting some paper processes remain. Barriers include infrastructure disparities and digital literacy. National policy via SIGE achieves majority digital use at rural facilities, but full rollout challenges yield score 3.

revision_notes: The Ministry of Education's own SIGE portal confirms nationwide completion of the platform's rollout to all 395 basic education schools by February 2019 (after all 43 secondary schools in 2018), used at school level for attendance, grades and administrative records with a parent-facing online dossier. This is clear, authoritative, facility-level evidence and corroborates the original score. It was considered whether this now supports the scale's top code (Entirely digital), but the evidence does not confirm that paper has been eliminated at the facility (e.g. attendance backups, exercise books, connectivity-driven fallback in the least-served islands), and the Afrobarometer survey continues to document a material rural-urban gap in device ownership and internet access that plausibly affects consistency of digital engagement in the most remote schools. The score is therefore confirmed at 3 rather than promoted to 4.
revised_comments: Cabo Verde's Sistema Integrado de Gestao Escolar (SIGE), developed by NOSi with the Ministry of Education, was rolled out to all 395 basic education schools nationwide by February 2019 (following completion in all 43 secondary schools in 2018), and is used at school level to record attendance, grades and administrative data, with a parent-facing portal ('Dossier do Aluno') accessible via the Porton di Nos Ilha government portal. This represents comprehensive digital data capture at the point of service across the school network, including rural islands. Afrobarometer survey data nonetheless show that rural and lower-income households have less reliable device ownership and internet access than urban households, a gap that can affect the consistency of digital engagement, for example during remote or e-learning provision, even where the school's own administrative system is digitised.
